why: The status VIEW is a renderer, not a source (ticfac tick 6dh). ticfac
watch (89m), the bare 'ticfac' listing (2qz), a phone page (i1r) and an
agent checking in all ask one run the same questions — does anything need
a person, is it healthy, how far along the whole epic, what is happening
now — and before this model each would have assembled its own answers from
the records, which is three hand-rolled watchers waiting to happen: the
exact failure the run event feed was built to end (tick u9l). One model,
versioned and stable, is what those surfaces render.
The model reads only what exists and adds no source of truth: the
tracker's graph for waves and tick identity, the run's durable records
(checkpoint, attempt markers, evidence, decisions, absorptions, findings)
for every state it states — never a worker's own claim — the event feed and
the liveness probes for hints and counts, the runner's session log for
worker silence (the signal tick b1t names), and the forge's check runs for
CI. A field with nothing behind it is null, never a guess: the model's
honesty rule is the same one every record under .ticfac/ holds.
This fixture lives beside the Go code because only Go reads it today. The
moment a second reader exists — the factory's TypeScript, for the phone
page — it moves to the pinned cross-language bundle the way every
two-reader contract does, and that move is the tick it files.
The dashboard fields (epic hn6, wave 1 — tick r5i) are ADDITIVE within
schema_version 1: the per-tick pipeline cell, parent, duration, findings
and report, the per-try tier/reason/next_step, the per-worker handle and
activity window, the health verdict, the per-source cost lines, recent,
epic_title and gloss. The `dashboard` golden carries every one of them
populated — it is the fixture the wave-3 renderers and the phone page
test against. The version does not move: the phone page's snapshot
parser refuses any model version other than 1, and every reader of this
contract lives in this repository.

layout.cardinality: exactly one object per invocation, whole
layout.exit_code_is: liveness's answer alone: 0 alive, 1 not alive, 2 usage — the model's content never changes it, so a script branching on status --json branches on the run's life
layout.stdout_carries: the model and nothing else, indented, one trailing newline

boundary.state_from: the durable records (checkpoint, attempt markers, evidence) and the tracker — never a worker's own claim
boundary.feed_is: hints and counts: waits say when, health counts what the run itself typed; no verdict is taken from a line
boundary.best_effort: a source that cannot be read costs the model that source's fields and a name in degraded, never the whole answer

checked_beyond_schema: a reader that meets a schema_version it does not know refuses the document rather than guessing at it

null and empty are different claims wherever the schema allows a null: waves null means the tracker could not be read, waves [] means it read and layered nothing; workers null means the census could not be taken (a cloud run), workers [] means no attempt stands
recent holds at most the last five feed lines, oldest first — the schema cannot count or order; the builder's test does
a cost line with metered false carries usd null — the anyOf pins it, the negative refuses it, and no renderer may print $0.00 for spend nobody measured

schema.description: One run's whole answer. Closed: a field this schema does not name is a field no reader parses, and a model that grows a field nobody versioned breaks its renderers silently. Every field that can be genuinely absent is required-and-null rather than omittable, the convention the bundle's provenance object established.

run_id.description: The run's id, the same one that names .ticfac/runs/<run-id>/.

epic_id.description: The epic the run runs. Empty when no record names it.

generated_at.description: RFC3339. Every age and elapsed the model states is measured against this one moment, so one answer carries one clock.

epic_title.description: The epic's own title, copied straight off the tracker's graph. Null when the graph could not be read — an unread tracker and a titleless epic are different claims, and only the first is a claim at all.

recent.description: The run's own last words: the last five lines of the feed, oldest first — the tail a dashboard shows where a watcher once drowned in the whole stream. The same event shape liveness.last_event carries. Empty, never null, when the feed is empty or unreadable.

waits_on.description: The one thing the run is blocked on. Null when nothing blocks it.

attention.description: Everything a person must do, in no order but the reader's own priority.

gates.description: The run's gate evidence, per check per head, exactly as the records state it.

ci.description: What the forge says on the epic PR's head, per check. Null when no PR exists or the forge could not be asked.

remaining.description: The approximate time left, only where measured tick durations support it. Null everywhere else — a number nobody measured is a number that lies.

schema_version.description: The model's version. A reader that meets a value it does not know refuses the document.

host.description: Where the run lives: a local run is named by its epic id, a cloud one by run_ plus hex and hosted by the factory.

degraded.description: Every source that could not be read, by the name the reader knows it by: tracker, run-state, feed, forge, worktree-census. Empty says every source answered. A source that answers none is NOT degraded — that is the source doing its job.

state.description: The probe's own vocabulary, carried verbatim: alive, dead, not_running, unknown for a local run; the Workflow's own state for a cloud one.

source.description: The probe's own name for where the answer came from: run.pid, workflow-record, workflow-supervisor.

last_event.description: The run's last word from its feed — a hint about when to look, never a verdict. Null when the feed is empty or unreadable.

last_event_age_seconds.description: The last event measured against generated_at, so a renderer never does clock arithmetic.

feed_event.description: One line of the run event feed, as the feed's own contract defines it (contracts/run-event-feed.json, ticfac.run_event.v1): carried here as the liveness hint it is.

phase.description: Where the epic stands. The merge is a person's by default (see .tick/config.md): everything up to it — a READY PR, kept ready as the base moves — is work a run can prove it did, and the merge is the judgement about whether to accept it. A repository may opt in to the run merging its own ready PR.

phases.description: Each phase's own state, in the fixed order plan, waves, review, closeout, ci, merge. No skipped: a phase the epic does not carry is done, because a phase that costs nothing is not one a renderer should show as waiting.

wave.description: Which wave the run is in and how many there are, when the run is in the waves phase. Null otherwise.

ticks.description: The epic's children counted. Null when the tracker could not be read.

waves.description: The waves counted; active is the frontier wave's own number, 0 when none is active. Null when the tracker could not be read.
Every wave of the epic with its ticks, from the same layering tk graph computes. Null when the tracker could not be read — no waves and unread waves are different claims.

state.description: done: every tick in it closed; active: the frontier wave; upcoming: behind the frontier.

title.description: The tracker's own title, for the person reading. Absent when the tracker states none.

gloss.description: The tracker's own one-line gloss, copied straight off the graph task. Absent when the tracker states none.

role.description: The tick's role (review, closeout) — the fact the lifecycle phases and the pipeline stage list derive from. Absent when the tick carries none.

state.description: The checkpoint's own closed vocabulary, from the durable records only — never a worker's own claim. The tracker's closed status backs it where the checkpoint has no row.

absorbed.description: The run itself created this tick by absorbing a finding into the epic it was running — the mid-run shape change a renderer shows as a marked row.

pipeline.description: The tick's own pipeline cell — the stages this role's tick passes through, each with its own state, the thing a dashboard fills left to right. The stage list is the role's: implement [claim, work, gate, merged], review [claim, review, closed], closeout [claim, work, ci, closed] — the same lists the Go builder spells as PipelineImplement, PipelineReview and PipelineCloseout.

parent_tick_id.description: The tick this row is indented under — a repair tick or an absorbed finding under its source tick. Null for a direct child of the epic: the rows never move, the children sit under their parent.

duration_seconds.description: From the tick's first dispatch to its close, or to generated_at while it is open. Null when no dispatch marker states a start.

findings.description: The findings this tick's report drafted — key, title and whether each gates. Empty when it drafted none.

report.description: The attempt report a person drills into: its own one-line summary and its diff stats. Null when the report was not read.

try.description: The tick's own try number of its current or last attempt (the h58 language: w9b#3 is the third try, not dispatch #3). Null when the records show no dispatch.

attempt.description: That attempt's run-wide dispatch number — its identity.

outcome.description: From the durable records alone: the checkpoint's word, then the gate evidence that dispatch produced, then the census.

dispatched_at.description: The attempt marker's own stamp. Empty when the marker could not be read — never guessed.

tier.description: This attempt's provenance tier — the rung of the ladder that routed the model. Null when no record states it.

reason.description: For an attempt that did not close, the record's own word for why — the sentence the dashboard shows instead of a bare "rejected ×n". Null when the attempt closed or nothing states why.

next_step.description: What the run did next, for an attempt that did not close — the answer to "and then what". Null on the same terms as reason.

tier.description: The current attempt's provenance tier — the rung of the ladder that routed the model.

elapsed_seconds.description: How long the current attempt has run, from its dispatch marker to generated_at. Null when the tick has no in-flight attempt.

pipeline.description: One tick's pipeline cell. The stage list is the role's own, in the order a tick passes through it: implement [claim, work, gate, merged]; review [claim, review, closed]; closeout [claim, work, ci, closed]. Spelled once in the Go builder (PipelineImplement, PipelineReview, PipelineCloseout) and once here, so the two cannot drift over a list one side never agreed to.

pipeline_stage.description: One stop of a tick's pipeline. The closed vocabulary across every role: claim, work, review, gate, ci, merged, closed — a stage outside it is a stage no renderer knows how to draw.

pipeline_state.description: One stage's own state: not reached, happening now, behind it, or refused there. Deliberately not the phase states — a stage can fail where a phase only moves on.

key.description: The finding's durable key — the same sha a triage addresses it by.

gating.description: Whether the finding gates the run's close-out. Null while nobody has triaged it yet — a draft has no answer, and null is that honest no-answer.

summary.description: The report's own one-line summary. Null when the report carried none.

diff.description: The report's diff as three counts. Null when the diff was not read.

workers.description: One entry per live worker. Null when the census cannot be taken (a cloud run's worktrees are not on this machine); empty when it read and nothing stands.

branch.description: The write ref the attempt owns.

worktree.description: The path git's registration names; empty when the attempt has no standing registration on this machine.

handle.description: The executor's own name for the worker — for example a herdr pane or agent name — the word a person uses to find it on the machine. Null when the executor named none.

activity.description: The worker's measured activity window: the sparkline a dashboard draws, the last action and when, the nudges the run sent. Null when nothing measured it.

branch_idle_seconds.description: How long since the branch last moved. Not a verdict — a worker thinking hard legitimately commits nothing for a while.

worktree_idle_seconds.description: How long since the worktree last changed.

detail.description: The run's own firing line, verbatim — what the executor was last seen doing.

wall_clock.description: The run's own typed statement that this attempt's wall clock fired. Null when the run said no such thing.

silence_seconds.description: How long since the runner's own session log last grew — pi appends on every turn, so the log's age is the worker's liveness (tick b1t). Null when the runner has no session log this machine can read.

last_turn.description: A one-line summary of the runner's last turn — the person's half, never parsed.

window_seconds.description: The width of the window the buckets cover.

buckets.description: One count per bucket, oldest first — the sparkline's own data.

last_action.description: The last tool action the worker took, as its transcript states it. Null when the transcript states none.

last_action_at.description: RFC3339, when the last action happened. Null on the same terms.

nudges.description: How many times the run nudged this worker for silence — stuck nudges made visible.

kind.description: The closed vocabulary of what a run can be blocked on.

what.description: The fact, in the words the record or line stated it in.

since.description: When the wait began, from the record or line that states it. Null when nothing states a moment.

needs_person.description: Only a person can move it. A wait that does not need one is a wait a watcher watches, not an alarm.

unblock_command.description: The one command that moves the wait on, when one exists and the wait needs a person. Null otherwise.

wait_nullable.description: The wait object, or null when nothing blocks the run. Inlined from $defs/wait rather than $ref'd so a wait kind outside the vocabulary is refused BY NAME — an anyOf would swallow the nested refusal and the pin exists to hold the vocabulary.

remote_retries.description: The run's own typed remote_retried lines, counted.

interventions.description: The interventions the run resumed by itself (resumed_automatically), counted.

verdict.description: The headline a dashboard answers "is it healthy" with — a word a person reads, not four counters they have to interpret. The raw counts stay beside it as the drill-in.

state.description:
The closed vocabulary of the headline.
- healthy: the run needs nobody and recovered what it hit
- degraded: something is wrong but the run is going
- stopped: the run is not going

summary.description: The one-line why beside the word — the sentence a person reads under the headline, empty when the word says it all.

recovered.description: What the run got past by itself, so it is shown as calm and not as alarms. Empty when nothing needed getting past.

what.description: The thing recovered from, named the way the run's own line names it.

seconds.description: How long the last one took, where anything measured it. Null when nothing did.

key.description: The evidence record's own key — the same name a JobResult citation carries.

check.description: The check's id, as the gate configured it.

phase.description: The gate vocabulary the record's provenance names — the same command at a different phase answers a different question.

head.description: The source sha the check ran on. Null when the record states none — a gate that names no head proves nothing about a ref.

state.description: The forge's own closed classification, the state the close-out's gate reads.

pr.description: The epic integration pull request — the thing the merge belongs to.

checks.description: The latest run of every check the forge recorded for the head — per check, the facts the classification derives from.

recorded_usd.description: What the records state about money: the decision records' own usage. The basis names the coverage so the number cannot quietly claim more than the records do.

attempts.description: How many dispatches the run paid for — the count a person multiplies by their own rates.

lines.description: The spend split per source: which river, whether anything measured it, the number where one exists. Empty when nothing has been split yet — and a line with no measurement states usd null and says so, never a fabricated $0.00.

anyOf.$comment: metered: a number exists or the reader truly has none yet
unmetered: there is no number to state, so there is none

source.description: Which river the line's spend ran through — the closed vocabulary the dashboard's cost row names.

metered.description: Whether anything measured this line's spend. False means the usd MUST be null: a number where nothing was measured is a fabricated spend.

usd.description: The measured spend, where it was measured. Null otherwise — the whole point of the field.

attempts.description: How many dispatches this line covers — the count a person multiplies by their own rates when nothing measured the money.

basis.description: Names what the number covers and where it came from, so it cannot quietly claim more than it does.

approximate_seconds.description: The median of what closed ticks measurably took, times the ticks still open.

basis.description: Names the estimate for what it is — approximate, and on what measured ground.
